summary.name: TimeScribe
summary.one_liner: TimeScribe is a free, open source, offline time tracker for macOS and Windows that records working hours, breaks, projects, and overtime locally without an account.
use_cases: Recording daily working hours and breaks for home office or flexible work
Spotting overtime or missed hours against a weekly schedule
Tracking billable client hours and exporting for invoices
Planning vacation and logging sick days
Automating timer start and stop with shortcuts or deeplinks
summary.what_it_does: TimeScribe tracks working hours, breaks, projects, and overtime, and stores all data locally on the device with no account required. It offers a menu bar timer for switching projects quickly, plus keyboard shortcuts and deeplinks for starting and controlling tracking. It supports a weekly work schedule, a working time balance, and absences including vacation allowance, sick days, and public holidays based on location. Projects can carry hourly rates, and time entries can be exported as CSV, Excel, or PDF. The page also describes optional app usage tracking (disabled by default) and automatic start/pause of tracking.
notable: Open source source code, so users can verify what the app does
Runs fully offline with all data stored locally, no cloud or account
Menu bar timer with keyboard shortcuts and deeplinks for automation
Absence management with vacation allowance, sick days, and location-based public holidays
caveats: Intentionally built for individual users, not teams; the page recommends OpenProject and other tools for teams
Available for macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows only; no other platforms are named
Interface is available in a limited set of languages, with more planned
